title: On the Geometric Emergence of the Electromagnetic Field in Teleparallel Spacetime
content: This study proposes a geometric interpretation of electromagnetism in four-dimensional teleparallel spacetime through the torsional structure of the temporal tetrad. The electromagnetic potential is treated not as an independent field externally added to spacetime, but as a deviation of the temporal tetrad from the background flow of time. Within this framework, the electromagnetic field is identified with the physical content of temporal torsion, and Maxwell theory is reformulated through a tetrad-geometric dictionary. Although the theory reproduces the physical content of the standard Maxwell equations and the Poisson limit in suitable weak-field or limiting regimes, it is not generally identical to Maxwell electrodynamics. Additional geometric terms arising from the torsional structure of the tetrad contribute to the electromagnetic kinetic sector and extend the field equations beyond the purely classical Maxwell form. The motion of charged particles remains compatible with the Lorentz force in the appropriate limit, while the Aharonovr–Bohm phase is interpreted as the global holonomy of the temporal tetrad. The framework also provides a geometric interpretation of the Reissnerr–Nordström metric. Strong-field systems, such as pulsars, are regarded as natural domains for discussing possible observational and astrophysical consequences of these torsional contributions.
